subject: general
question: The angle formed by the backward tilt of the steering axis from vertical, when viewed from the side of the wheel is known as __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __positive castor**(Option 1)**.__

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• Positive castor__ refers to the backward tilt of the steering axis from the vertical when viewed from the side.
 
• It is a crucial alignment setting in vehicles that impacts steering stability.
 
• A positive castor angle improves straight-line stability and helps the wheels return to the straight-ahead position after turning.
 
• This alignment is commonly used in modern vehicles to enhance handling and control.
 
• The castor angle is measured in degrees and can be adjusted during vehicle servicing.
 
• Incorrect castor settings can lead to poor handling and uneven tire wear.

**__Additional Information__**

 
• **Camber Angle:**

 
 
• The camber angle is the tilt of the wheel from the vertical, viewed from the front or rear.
 
• Positive camber means the top of the wheel is tilted outward.
 
 
 
• **Toe Angle:**
 
 
• The toe angle is the direction the wheels are pointed relative to the longitudinal axis of the vehicle.
 
• It is classified as toe-in (wheels closer at the front) or toe-out (wheels closer at the rear).
 
 
 
• **Steering Axis Inclination:**
 
 
• Steering axis inclination (SAI) is the inward tilt of the suspension's steering pivot points.
 
• It enhances vehicle stability and reduces steering effort.
